correctness.rationale: The Laurent series Phi(z)=exp[(a/2)(z^p+z^-p)+(b/2)(z^q+z^-q)] has real symmetric coefficients; multiplying by exp(-a-b)>0 preserves their signs. For a,b>=0, the convergent modified-Bessel convolution is termwise positive on the active gcd lattice and zero elsewhere. Necessity is the crucial nonstandard step: finitely many negative Laurent coefficients could be canceled by a Laurent polynomial P with nonnegative coefficients, forcing |Phi(re^{i theta})|<=Phi(r)+2P(r). If b<0, theta=pi/q makes the leading q-harmonic grow exponentially whereas Phi(r)+2P(r) is only polynomial. If b>0,a<0, theta=2pi/q leaves positive q-growth unchanged while enhancing the negative p-growth by exp(c r^p), overwhelming P(r)/Phi(r)->0. If b=0,a<0 use theta=pi/p. This exhausts all boundaries. The Fourier/Bochner criterion and Vandermonde system in e^{id x_j} prove necessity and exact strictness for arbitrary finite distinct sites modulo 2pi/d. Independently checked selected Bessel/Fourier coefficients and negative signed examples; those finite samples are not an all-frequency proof.
residual_risks: Finite independently reconstructed numerical checks do not establish infinite-parameter assertions; the mathematical proof is necessary.

final_claim: For integer 1<=p<q and a,b real, exp(a(cos(pt)-1)+b(cos(qt)-1)) is positive definite on all finite circle-site configurations iff a,b>=0. Every forbidden signed parameter pair yields infinitely many negative Fourier coefficients; positive coefficients have exactly the active-frequency gcd lattice support and the indicated quotient-circle strictness.
